questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: How fast the material must be delivered.

questions.correctAnswerText: What dangers the material has.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are sorted into nine classes. Each class describes the type of danger the material poses.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials containers, do not use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hooks.
questions.explanation: Protect hazardous materials containers. Never use equipment like hooks that could damage containers or packaging.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turned off.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading a tank with flammable liquids. The only exception is if you need the engine running to operate a pump. Ground the tank before opening it and keep it grounded until after closing.

questions.question: Your shipment may contain hazardous materials if:

options.text: The company deals in fireworks or explosives.
Your last pickup was labeled as hazardous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The company deals in fireworks or explosives.
questions.explanation: One clue is the shipper's business type. Companies that deal in hazardous materials include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, scientific supply houses, pest control businesses, farms, and fireworks or explosives dealers.

questions.question: Shippers package hazardous materials to ____ them.
questions.correctAnswerText: Contain
questions.explanation: Shippers package hazardous materials to fully contain them. Vehicles must display placards that show what cargo risks are present.

questions.question: If shipping papers say "Inhalation Hazard":

options.text: Use an inhalation hazard placard only if carrying more than 100 pounds.
Use an inhalation hazard placard for any amount of the material.
Provide air masks to everyone handling the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use an inhalation hazard placard for any amount of the material.
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a package or shipping paper, display the proper inhalation hazard placards and any other required placards. This applies no matter how much material you are carrying.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, a driver must have:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
A CDL with a tank endorsement
A CDL with a cargo endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: A shipping paper:

options.text: Is not needed for most hazardous materials shipments.
Is required for all hazardous materials shipments.
Can be stored only in a digital file.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required for all hazardous materials shipments.
questions.explanation: Shippers must provide shipping papers for all hazardous materials. These papers communicate the risks of the materials.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Always watch the nozzle and control the fuel flow during refueling.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained?

options.text: At least once every three years

questions.correctAnswerText: At least once every three years
questions.explanation: Employees who work with hazardous materials must receive training and pass a test at least once every three years.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be kept?

options.text: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous materials, keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or another spot the driver can reach easily while wearing a seat belt. Papers must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Which material may need a transport index?
questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials must have a transport index. This number shows how much control the material needs during transport. All cargo in one vehicle cannot have a combined transport index over 50.

questions.question: Many poison products are also:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flammable.
questions.explanation: Many hazardous materials that are poisonous are also flammable.

questions.question: Who must label hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper
questions.explanation: The shipper must properly package, mark, and label hazardous materials. The driver should check that materials are labeled correctly.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, you should know:

options.text: Radiation spreads from the package and reaches other packages nearby.
The package should be transported in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation spreads from the package and reaches other packages nearby.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads from each radioactive package and reaches all nearby packages. The number of packages loaded together is controlled to prevent this.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a small truck fire, you should:

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.
questions.explanation: Before opening trailer doors during a truck fire, feel them to check if they are hot. Hot doors may mean there is a cargo fire. Keep doors closed if there is a cargo fire.

questions.question: Where must hazardous materials placards be placed?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the outside of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle when required.

questions.question: What sign shows a shipment may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo comes from a supermarket.
The cargo is on wood pallets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often hold hazardous materials. Take proper precautions if transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: When can an improperly placarded vehicle be moved?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: In an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper placards cannot be driven except in emergencies to protect life or property.

questions.question: What must a box display if it contains liquid containers?

options.text: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Boxes with liquid containers must have orientation markers. Arrows on the box must point in the correct upright direction.

questions.question: What can you do with an improperly placarded vehicle?

options.text: You can only move it in an emergency.
You can drive it if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only move it in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper placards for hazardous materials cannot be driven. The only exception is when it is necessary to move it to protect people and property during an emergency.

questions.question: If a shipping paper says "Inhalation Hazard," what placard should the shipper use?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a shipping paper or package, you must display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: How many identical placards must be on a vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle must have four identical placards. Place one on the front, one on the back, and one on each side.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, what should you do with the liquid discharge valves?
questions.correctAnswerText: Open them.
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank closed at all times except when loading or unloading.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for hazardous chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
questions.explanation: The Department of Transportation (DOT) Emergency Response Guide lists information about hazardous materials. You can find them by proper shipping names and hazardous materials identification numbers.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.3 materials, what should the floor liner be made from?
questions.correctAnswerText: Non-ferrous materials.
questions.explanation: When transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials, use a floor liner made from non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal. Non-ferrous metals do not contain iron.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, what should you do with the liquid discharge valves?
questions.correctAnswerText: Open them.
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank closed at all times except when loading or unloading.

questions.question: If a driver stops and leaves their vehicle while carrying hazardous materials, where should the shipping papers be?

options.text: Left in the front seat of the cab.
Placed in a box under the passenger seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left in the front seat of the cab.
questions.explanation: If a driver stops and gets out of the vehicle, the hazardous materials shipping papers must stay on the driver's seat.

questions.question: What is the only reliable way to check tire pressure?
questions.correctAnswerText: With a tire pressure gauge.
questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only accurate way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: When you apply for a new or renewed HazMat endorsement, which agency does the background check?
questions.correctAnswerText: The Transportation Security Administration
questions.explanation: When you apply for a new or renewed HazMat endorsement, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) performs a federal security background check.
